title: Normalized whole-system coefficient and compact-support comparison models
statement: Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Let $I$ be its directed set of finite coefficient subfields [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. For $E\le F$ in $I$, coefficient data comprise the actual maps $\mathcal O_E/\ell^{n+1}\to\mathcal O_F/\ell^{n+1}$ induced by the integral inclusion [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined], and the corresponding natural transformations of the constant sheaf ring towers [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Let $a_T$ be their morphism of rings on the sequence site and let scalar models be the ordinary and K-flat-normalized derived extension/restriction adjunctions [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized pullback comparison consists of: the coefficient-restriction/geometric-pushforward isomorphism which is identity on every section; the ordinary scalar/geometric-pullback isomorphism whose double adjunction mate is that restriction comparison; and its derived isomorphism characterized by the same map on every K-flat cochain representative. A model family consists, for every $E$, of the specified tower operations [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] and [det-sp-reduction-direct-image], and the section-preserving evaluation and scalar coordinates with their derived realization [def-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-interfaces], and for every inclusion of fields of these scalar models, normalized pullback comparisons, and open-extension scalar isomorphisms whose inverses are the mates of the inverse pullback comparisons under the open adjunctions. For a compactification $X\xrightarrow j Z\xrightarrow hY$, define the proper coefficient comparison to be the actual adjunction mate of the scalar/pullback square, and define $b$ as that mate after $j_!$, followed by $Rh_*$ of the open scalar comparison. Define the normalized constructible predicate by transport of [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers] along the recorded section-preserving equivalence. These are definitions and normalization data, without asserting their existence or any invertibility or cocycle law for $b$.
